lines: Stereo compressor with meters for input, gain reduction and output, and a side chain input that can drive the detector in place of the signal
Multiplies the input by 0 to 4 before the detector reads it, despite the tooltip calling it Fade In Speed
Multiplies the compressed signal by 0 to 8, and the result is clipped at 6V, despite the tooltip calling it Fade In Speed
Sets the level the signal has to pass before the gain is pulled down, 6V fully counter-clockwise falling to a hundredth of that fully clockwise, despite the tooltip calling it Fade In Speed
Sets how far the gain is pulled down past the threshold: 0 leaves it alone, 1 closes it completely, past 1 the gain passes through zero and the signal inverts, though its tooltip says Fade In Speed
Sets how long the gain takes to reach full reduction after the signal crosses the threshold, 0 to 500ms
Sets how long the gain takes to come back after the signal falls under the threshold, 0 to 2 seconds, despite the tooltip calling it Fade In Speed
Multiplies the side chain input by 0 to 1 before the detector reads it, despite the tooltip calling it Fade In Speed
The left channel in, summed across its polyphony channels
The right channel in, summed across its polyphony channels
A cable here makes the detector follow this signal instead of the left and right inputs, while the left and right carry the gain the detector calls for
The compressed left channel, clipped at 6V
The compressed right channel, clipped at 6V
Note — the Bypass switch passes the inputs straight to the outputs, skipping the input gain, the compressor and the output gain
Compressor1.notes: Parameter 6 is configured as the bypass but carries no widget; the Bypass switch on the panel is a custom button rather than a parameter, so parameter 6 is left untagged. Every parameter carries the tooltip name 'Fade In Speed', which is a copy-and-paste slip in the maker's source; the lines follow the panel lettering and the code instead.

lines: Four clock channels driven by one tempo, each multiplying or dividing it, with a sync input per channel and a chain jack for handing the tempo to another of these
Sets the main tempo, 60 to 220 beats per minute
Multiplies or divides the main tempo for that channel, from divide by 32, through unity, to multiply by 32
A rising edge here restarts that channel's clock on the next main beat
Takes the tempo and the run state from another MSC Clock, and while a cable is here the BPM knob is ignored
A 1ms 10V pulse at that channel's rate, silent while that channel or the whole module is stopped
A 1ms 10V pulse each time that channel is resynchronised
Carries this module's tempo and run state for another MSC Clock to follow
Nothing in the module applies this knob; a jitter value is computed from it and then never added to the clock
MasterClockx4.notes: Parameter 5, Humanize, is left untagged: the line that would apply it to the beat counter is commented out in the source, so the knob does nothing. The STOP, GLOBAL, SYNC and x2 controls are custom buttons rather than parameters. The four CLOCK jacks of a channel carry the same pulse, as do its four SYNC TRIGs jacks.

lines: Nine envelope generators sharing one drawable editor, each timed from the patched clock and each with its own trigger and hold input
Sets how far the points either side of a dragged point follow it, the pull falling to under two thirds at each step away; at zero only the dragged point moves
The clock every envelope is timed from, one edge to the next setting the length of a beat; with nothing patched here no channel produces an envelope
A rising edge here restarts every envelope at the start of its shape
A rising edge here retriggers all nine envelopes at once
Held above 2.5V this freezes that channel's envelope at its current value
A rising edge here retriggers that channel's envelope from the start of its shape
That channel's envelope, over the range picked by the Out Range switch: 0-5V, -5V to 5V, 0-10V or -10V to 10V
SEQ_Envelope_8.notes: The channel selector, the envelope mode, the time division, the output range, Draw, Gate View, Invert, Smooth, Presets, Rand and Copy are custom widgets rather than parameters, so they carry no line.

lines: Three keyboard sequencers, each with its own clock, sixteen steps, sixteen patterns and a three-octave keyboard for setting the note of each step
Sets how long the pitch takes to slide from the previous note to the new one on a step marked for glide, up to 500ms
A rising edge here advances that row one step; with nothing patched, the row follows the clock of the first row
Adds its voltage to that row's pitch output, transposing the pattern
A rising edge here queues the next pattern for that row, which takes effect when the row reaches its first step
A rising edge here returns every row to the first step of its pattern
A rising edge here queues the next pattern on all three rows
Held above 0V this silences the trigger output of every row and freezes every pitch output at its last note
Held above 0V this silences that row's trigger output and freezes its pitch output at its last note
A 50ms 10V pulse on each step the pattern marks with a note
The pitch of that row's current step, a volt per octave, with the row's octave setting and its V/Oct offset input added
Menu — Ch 1, Ch 2 and Ch 3 Reset Pattern to 1 make a clock reset return that row to its first pattern as well as its first step
TriadSeq2.notes: Parameters 0 to 17 and 21 to 23 are declared in the source but never configured and carry no widget, so they are left untagged. The keyboards, step and pattern strips, pause, copy, octave select and the mute buttons are custom widgets rather than parameters.

lines: Seven-note arpeggiator with sixteen patterns, three sub-steps per note, note lengths from a whole note down to a thirty-second, and glide and legato per note
The clock the arpeggio runs from; with nothing patched here the trigger output stays at 0V and the pattern does not advance
A rising edge here restarts the pattern at its first note
Adds its voltage to the pitch output, transposing the arpeggio
A rising edge here queues the next pattern, which takes effect at the start of the next pass
A 10V gate for as long as the current note lasts, dropped one tick early so consecutive notes do not run together
The pitch of the current note, a volt per octave, with the pattern's octave setting and the V/OCT offset input added, and sliding over 200ms on a note marked for glide
ARP700.notes: This module has no parameters at all: the keyboard, the pattern strip, the octave select, the on/off, note length, length modifier, glide, legato, pause and copy buttons and the mode strip are custom widgets.

lines: Six trigger sequencers of up to 32 steps, each with sixteen patterns and five level knobs a step can draw its CV from
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the lowest of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the second of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the middle of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the fourth of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the highest of the five levels
A rising edge here advances that row one step; with nothing patched, the row follows the clock of the first row
A rising edge here queues the next pattern for that row, which takes effect when the row reaches its first step
A rising edge here returns every row to its first step
A rising edge here queues the next pattern on all six rows
Held above 0V this silences every trigger output and freezes every CV output at its last value
A 1ms 10V pulse on each step the pattern marks
The level of the current step scaled to the full range set on the menu, or a bipolar version of it when the Bi-Dir switch for that row is on
A 1ms 10V pulse each time that row returns to its first step
Menu — VRange sets the full scale of every CV output to 15V, 10V or 5V
Seq_6ch_32step.notes: The step grid, the pattern strip, pause, Cpy, Rand, CLR, Gate and Bi-Dir are custom widgets rather than parameters.

lines: Three synth voices in one module, each stacking up to seven detuned copies of one waveform through an envelope and a multimode filter into a stereo pair
Sets how long that voice takes to climb to full level after a trigger, from under 1ms to 2 seconds
Sets how long that voice holds at full level before it starts to fall, up to 4 seconds
Sets how long that voice takes to fall back to silence, up to 10 seconds
Sets how many copies of the waveform that voice stacks, 1 to 7
Spreads the stacked copies of that voice apart in pitch, all at the same pitch at zero
Spreads the stacked copies of that voice apart across the stereo pair, all centred at zero
Sets the cutoff of that voice's filter
Sets the resonance of that voice's filter
Picks the filter for that voice: off, low pass, high pass, band pass or notch
Sets the output level of that voice, full giving 6V
Sets the pitch of that voice, a volt per octave with 0V giving 32.7Hz, and voltages above 8V clamped
A rising edge here restarts that voice's envelope from silence
Attenuates the filter cutoff knob of that voice, 10V leaving the knob where it is and 0V closing the filter; an empty jack reads 10V
Attenuates the filter resonance knob of that voice, 10V leaving the knob where it is; an empty jack reads 10V
Adds to the output level knob of that voice, 5V covering the whole of the knob's range
The left side of that voice
The right side of that voice
Note — each voice plays one of five waveforms, chosen with its own button strip: sine, triangle, square, saw or noise
Osc_3Ch_Widget.notes: Parameters 9 to 26 are configured as 'Not Used' and carry no widget, so they are left untagged. The waveform button strip for each voice is a custom widget rather than a parameter.

lines: Oscillator crossfading between three waveforms you draw by hand, through a multimode filter and a level stage
Sets how far the points either side of a dragged point follow it, the pull falling to under two thirds at each step away; at zero only the dragged point moves
Sets the cutoff of the filter
Sets the resonance of the filter
Picks the filter: off, low pass, high pass, band pass or notch
Sets the output level
Sets the pitch, a volt per octave with 0V giving 32.7Hz and voltages above 8V clamped; an empty jack reads 4V
Crossfades between the three drawn waveforms, -5V for the first, 0V for the second and 5V for the third, despite the panel printing -10V, 0V and 10V
Attenuates the filter cutoff knob, 10V leaving the knob where it is and 0V closing the filter; an empty jack reads 10V
Attenuates the filter resonance knob, 10V leaving the knob where it is; an empty jack reads 10V
Attenuates the level knob, 10V leaving the knob where it is and 0V silencing the output; an empty jack reads 10V
While Solo is on, a rising edge here steps to the next of the three waveforms
The oscillator output
OSC_WaveMorph_3.notes: The panel prints -10V, 0V and 10V beside the Morph input, but the code divides that input by 5, so the first and third waveforms are reached at -5V and 5V. Draw, Solo, Invert, Presets, Rand and Copy are custom widgets rather than parameters.

lines: Stereo delay of up to 4 seconds a side, with feedback in both directions, a multimode filter across the input and a switch that plays the buffer backwards
Sets the left delay time, up to 4 seconds; with a clock at SYNC CLK the time is quantised to a division of that clock's period
Sets the right delay time, up to 4 seconds; with a clock at SYNC CLK the time is quantised to a division of that clock's period
Sets how much of the left delayed signal is fed back into the left delay
Sets how much of the left delayed signal is fed into the right delay
Sets how much of the right delayed signal is fed into the left delay
Sets how much of the right delayed signal is fed back into the right delay
Sets the cutoff of the filter the input passes through, ahead of both the delay line and the dry path
Sets the resonance of the filter the input passes through
Picks the filter: off, low pass, high pass, band pass or notch
Crossfades between the filtered input and the delayed signal
The left input, summed across its polyphony channels, and the source for both delays when the right input is empty
The right input, summed across its polyphony channels
A clock here quantises both delay times to a division of its period, the division taken from each delay knob's setting
A rising edge here switches the delay between playing its buffer forwards and backwards
The left output, the filtered input and the left delay mixed by MIX
The right output, the filtered input and the right delay mixed by MIX
PingPong_Widget.notes: Parameter 10 is configured as 'Unused' and carries no widget, so it is left untagged; the GNIP GNOP switch beside its input is a custom button rather than a parameter.

lines: Four delay taps in series clocked from a beat input, each with a note length, level, pan and feedback of its own, and a multimode filter on the way into the delay line
Picks the filter: off, low pass, high pass, band pass or notch
Sets the cutoff of the filter the signal passes through on its way into the delay line
Sets the resonance of the filter the signal passes through on its way into the delay line
Sets the level of that tap in the delayed mix
Sets the position of that tap between the left and right outputs
Sets how much of that tap is fed back into the delay line
Sets the length of that tap as a note value, off, two bars, a bar, a half, a quarter, an eighth, a sixteenth or a thirty-second, counted on from where the tap before it landed
Crossfades between the unfiltered input and the sum of the four taps
The clock the note lengths are measured against, one edge to the next counting as a quarter note
The left input, and the source for both sides when the right input is empty
The right input
Adds to the filter cutoff knob, 5V covering the whole of the knob's range and -5V closing the filter
The left output, the dry input and the delayed taps mixed by Mix
The right output, the dry input and the delayed taps mixed by Mix
Note — a tap set to Off is skipped, and the taps after it are measured from where the last sounding tap landed
StepDelay.notes: Input 1, Clock Reset, is declared in the source but never placed on the panel and never read, so it is left untagged. The Dotted and Triplet buttons under each tap are custom widgets rather than parameters.

lines: Eight stereo fade gates, each raising and lowering its pair of channels on a gate, with its own fade-in and fade-out times
Sets how long that row takes to fade up once its gate goes high, 0.05 to 40 seconds
Sets how long that row takes to fade down once its gate goes low, 0.05 to 40 seconds
A gate above 0.01V fades that row up and dropping it fades the row down; with nothing patched the jack reads high, leaving the row to its button
The left input of that row, passed through the row's fade
The right input of that row, passed through the row's fade
The left input of that row after the fade, or the fade shape itself as 0-10V when that input is empty
The right input of that row after the fade, or the fade shape itself as 0-10V when that input is empty
Note — a row whose fade is reversed part way through picks up from where it had reached rather than jumping
ASAF8.notes: The outputs carry whatever is patched into the row, and the fade envelope itself when nothing is, so they are left without a family. The fade button on each row is a custom widget rather than a parameter.

lines: Three morphing oscillators whose waveforms, detuning and modulation shapes are all built from a 32-bit seed, filtered and reverberated into a stereo pair
Sets how fast the modulation shapes run, in nine steps from a hundredth of their built-in rate to eight times it
Sets the pitch of the drone, a volt per octave with 0V giving 32.7Hz and voltages above 8V clamped; an empty jack reads 3V
A rising edge here picks a new random seed, and the drone fades out and back in on the new one
The left side of the drone
The right side of the drone
Note — the seed is set with the grid of 32 buttons, each one a bit of the seed, and the Random button rolls a new one
Two oscillators built from a 32-bit seed, one stepping through a bit pattern and one through a note sequence, each filtered by its own modulation shapes
Sets how fast the modulation shapes run, in nine steps from a hundredth of their built-in rate to eight times it
A cable here gates the module: the output is 0V whenever this input is at 0V, and the sound runs whenever it is above that
A rising edge here picks a new random seed, and the sound fades out and back in on the new one
The two oscillators mixed together
Note — the seed is set with the grid of 32 buttons, each one a bit of the seed, and the Random button rolls a new one
Three channels of noise built from a 32-bit seed, each with looping random shapes driving its level, filter cutoff and resonance, mixed to a stereo pair
Sets how fast the random shapes run, in nine steps from a hundredth of their built-in rate to eight times it
A rising edge here picks a new random seed, and the noise fades out and back in on the new one
The left side of the noise, the first and second channels summed
The right side of the noise, the first and third channels summed
Note — the seed is set with the grid of 32 buttons, each one a bit of the seed, and the Random button rolls a new one
Turns typed text into morse code, played out as gates once a trigger starts it
Sets the rate of the code, fully clockwise giving a dot a third of the length it has fully counter-clockwise
A rising edge here starts the message from its first character; the message plays once and then stops until the next edge
10V for the length of each dot and dash, 0V through the gaps between them
Note — the message is typed into the text field, and any character without a morse equivalent is skipped
Lorenz attractor run at audio rate, with its three coordinates mixed into one output through a multimode filter, and a display of the path it traces
Sets how much of the X coordinate goes into the output, 0 to 10 times
Sets how much of the Y coordinate goes into the output, 0 to 10 times
Sets how much of the Z coordinate goes into the output, 0 to 10 times
Sets the cutoff of the filter on the output
Attenuates the voltage at the cutoff CV input before it is added to the cutoff knob
Sets the resonance of the filter on the output
Attenuates the voltage at the resonance CV input before it is added to the resonance knob
Sets one of the three constants of the attractor equations, 0.1 at the counter-clockwise end rising to 40.1 at the clockwise end
Attenuates the voltage at the CV input for that constant before it is added to its knob
Sets the step size of one of the three attractor equations, the divisor running from 50 at the counter-clockwise end to 550 at the clockwise end
Attenuates the voltage at the CV input for that step size before it is added to its knob
Adds to the knob for that attractor constant, 5V covering the whole of its range, scaled by the attenuator for that constant
Adds to the knob for that step size, 5V covering the whole of its range, scaled by the attenuator for that step size
Adds to the filter cutoff knob, 5V covering the whole of its range, scaled by the cutoff attenuator
Adds to the filter resonance knob, 5V covering the whole of its range, scaled by the resonance attenuator
The three coordinates summed and scaled, DC removed, filtered, and clipped at 10V
Note — the Lo, Band and Hi buttons pick which output the filter takes, and with none of them lit the filter is bypassed
Clips, rectifies and combines two signals with one of five operations, then rectifies the result again and applies gain and a DC offset
Clips signal A to this voltage, 1V to 10V, before it is rectified
Clips signal B to this voltage, 1V to 10V, before it is rectified
Attenuates the CV added to the A clipping level
Attenuates the CV added to the B clipping level
Picks how A and B combine: their sum, their difference, the sine of A times the cosine of B, whichever of the two is smaller in size, or whichever is larger, though the panel prints Sin(A) + Cos(B)
Multiplies the combined signal by 0 to 2
Adds a fixed -5V to 5V to the output
The A signal, clipped at the A limit and then rectified by the A Rectify switch; with B unpatched the output carries A alone
The B signal, clipped at the B limit and then rectified by the B Rectify switch; with A unpatched the output carries B alone
Adds to the A clipping level, through its attenuator, and the result is held between -5V and 5V
Adds to the B clipping level, through its attenuator, and the result is held between -5V and 5V
The combined signal after the output rectifier, the gain and the DC offset, and 0V while neither input is patched
Maude221.notes: The panel prints the third combine position as Sin(A) + Cos(B), but the code multiplies the two rather than adding them. The three Rectify switches are custom widgets rather than parameters.

Mix_24_4_4.notes: The group strips carry left and right input jacks in the code that the panel hides and the audio path never reads; they are left untagged. The MUTE, SOLO, pre-fader and group-route buttons are custom widgets rather than parameters, so they carry no line.
